summary: Tenant accuracy drop + 95p latency spike after enabling aggressive batching and mixed quant profile; need rollback checklist and telemetry gaps
description:
Issue summary: Customer LuminaHealth reports simultaneous model accuracy degradation and 95th-percentile latency increase after we enabled an aggressive dynamic-group batching policy and applied a per-tenant mixed INT8/INT4 quantization profile during a staged rollout. Impact: Several production routes (chat and completion endpoints) for the tenant show reduced answer quality on an internal evaluation corpus (precision drop ~6%) and 95p latency rose from ~280ms to ~850ms across the tenant's busiest backends. This started after a targeted optimizer push at 02:15 UTC.

Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant pinned to model versions: llama-3-70b-chat@v2.18, optimizer profile: tenant-lumina-mixed-031426.

Observed behavior / timeline:
- 02:12 UTC: rollout start (canary batch to 5% of traffic).
- 02:20 UTC: anomalies appear in telemetry (95p latency drift + K/V eviction churn).
- 02:40 UTC: profile pushed to 30% traffic; complaints from customer at ~02:55 UTC.
- 03:05 UTC: customer reports lower answer relevance on their test set.

Immediate customer impact: Potential user-facing regressions for clinical suggestion flows; customer paused business-critical automation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated cluster us-east-1, enable dynamic-group batching with window=40ms and max_group=64 for tenant ID 0xA4
2) Apply quantization profile 'tenant-lumina-mixed-031426' (per-layer INT8 except attention projections INT4, prefix cache enabled)
3) Route 30% of live traffic through the profile via staged rollout, monitor 95p latency and eval set accuracy
4) Observe K/V eviction rate and tail latency metrics within 10-30 minutes
logs_and_metrics: Alert window: tracer:latency.95p (tenant=0xA4) increased from 280ms -> 850ms between 02:15-02:45 UTC
Model quality snapshot: internal-eval:precision@5 fell from 0.78 -> 0.73 on LuminaClinicalQA set
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching increased queueing for long-tail requests while mixed INT4 on attention projections created occasional token-level quality regressions for critical prompts.

Telemetry gap: we do not currently record per-tenant per-layer quant error rates or a per-request quant-fallback flag; suggested instrumentation to add: 'quant-fallback' tag and per-layer error counters.
Observed high KV eviction churn coinciding with dynamic-group batching; eviction spikes correlate with sequences >1024 tokens where cache entries are being evicted prematurely.

CPU/GPU utilization on dedicated nodes: GPU utilization remained moderate (48-62%) while host CPU saw scheduling spikes when batch windows shipped — indicates scheduler contention rather than pure GPU overload.
Repro check on staging with same profile produced similar quality drop on 12/20 test prompts focused on numeric reasoning and code snippets (sensitive to attention quantization).
workaround_suggested: 1) Immediately roll back staged rollout to previous optimizer profile (tenant-lumina-stable-0212) for all live traffic (stop at control plane).
2) Set per-tenant batching to conservative: window=10ms and max_group=16 as a temporary safe baseline.
3) Disable INT4 attention projection override for this tenant and re-enable INT8 for all layers until further testing.
4) Apply a temporary circuit-breaker: if 95p latency > 600ms for 5 consecutive minutes, auto-fallback to last-known-good profile.
5) Ask customer to run a focused prompt eval (12 prompts) after rollback to validate quality restored before full traffic resumption.
planned_resolution: Short term (next 3 hours): execute rollback steps 1-3 above, validate customer eval, and monitor 95p latency for 30 minutes.
Medium term (48-72 hours): add per-tenant quant-fallback telemetry and build a canary guard that blocks INT4 attention for routes flagged as 'sensitive'.

Long term: update optimizer rollout playbook to require an automated small-batch A/B evaluation (quality + 95p latency) for mixed-quant profiles and add a KB entry for tenant-specific rollback commands.

Miguel Ortiz (SRE) @ 2026-03-14T04:02Z: Rollback executed to tenant-lumina-stable-0212; initial validation shows 95p latency back to ~300ms. Asking for 30m monitor window before closing ticket.

resolution_notes: Action taken: Rolled back optimizer profile to tenant-lumina-stable-0212; reduced batching window and removed INT4 attention override for the tenant.
Immediate outcome: 95p latency returned to baseline (~300ms) and internal eval precision reverted to 0.77 (within noise of previous 0.78).
Follow-ups: Engineering to add quant-fallback telemetry, and Product to add a guard that blocks attention-INT4 for routes labeled 'sensitive'.
Postmortem owner: Miguel Ortiz (SRE) assigned, draft due 2026-03-18.
